report.summary: Analyzed fanout.py chunk 2 of 2; verified docstring and comment claims against code.
risks: line 316 | medium | The guard error message includes guard_error but does not include the original exception traceback; debugging failures may be harder. | Check if traceback is logged elsewhere or if the guard_error string should contain more detail.

line 350 | medium | The code catches Exception in the callback on_result; silently ignoring exceptions may hide bugs in the callback. | Consider logging the exception or providing a way for the caller to be notified.

handoff.purpose: Implement fan_out function: run tasks, handle resume, enforce budget guard, refuse deterministic votes, return summary dict.

symbols.name: fan_out
symbols.note: Main entry point; runs tasks, returns summary dict with state 'refused' or 'ran'.

symbols.name: _brief_for
symbols.note: Generates brief string from task paths using render_brief.

symbols.name: _run_task
symbols.note: Executes a single task: resumes from file or runs votes, writes result atomically.

symbols.name: counts
symbols.note: Local dict tracking ok, failed, resumed, calls.

symbols.name: lock
symbols.note: Threading lock for synchronizing counts and results.

symbols.name: guard_error
symbols.note: Error message from guard installation failure.

claims.text: Never raises for a failing task: a fan-out of 1,200 in which one task dies must produce 1,199 answers and a named failure, not an exception.
claims.why: All task exceptions are caught in the try/except around fut.result() (line 366-371) and converted to FanoutResult with errors. The function always returns a dict, never raises.

claims.text: Transport failures are recorded on the result and the queue continues
claims.why: Exceptions from _one_call are caught (line 334-336) and appended to res.errors. The loop continues for remaining votes. Also, exceptions in the callback on_result are caught (line 381-383).

claims.text: the summary reports ``failed`` separately from ``ok`` rather than folding them into a rate.
claims.why: Returned dict has separate 'ok' and 'failed' keys (lines 398-399).

claims.text: ``resume`` skips any task whose result file already exists AND parses. A file that exists but does not parse is re-run, because a truncated result is worse than a missing one: it looks like an answer.
claims.why: In _run_task (lines 319-326), if resume and dest.is_file(), it tries to json.loads; if that succeeds and res.answers is non-empty, it returns the resumed result. On OSError or ValueError, it falls through to re-run.

claims.text: asking for votes you cannot get is an error at the door
claims.why: Lines 305-316 check if any task.votes > 1 and temperature <= 0.0, and return a 'refused' dict immediately.

claims.text: At temperature 0.0 the decode is deterministic, so every vote returns the SAME answer
claims.why: The check on line 305 enforces that votes>1 requires temperature>0.

claims.text: THE GUARD, FIRST, BEFORE ANY CALL CAN LEAVE. Not conditional, not a parameter.
claims.why: The guard installation happens at lines 320-325, before any task submission (ThreadPoolExecutor at line 354). It is not conditional (always attempted) and not a parameter (hardcoded import).

claims.text: Fail CLOSED: a fan-out whose spend cannot be capped does not run
claims.why: If guard installation fails, the function returns a 'refused' dict (lines 332-345) without submitting any tasks.

claims.text: SAME SUMMARY SHAPE as a completed run, including `paid_calls` and `results`
claims.why: The 'refused' dict (lines 337-345) has the same keys as the 'ran' dict (lines 393-403): state, tasks, ok, failed, resumed, paid_calls, out_dir, concurrency, results.

claims.text: Resolved ONCE for the whole fan-out: every answer in one run belongs to that run.
claims.why: trace is resolved once at lines 347-351 and then used in _run_task (line 330) for all tasks.

claims.text: NOT re-stamped: the prior trace is the run that paid for this answer. Overwriting it with the current run's id would claim this run produced something it read off disk.
claims.why: In the resume path (line 325), the resumed FanoutResult uses prior.get('trace_id') instead of the current trace, preserving the original trace.

claims.text: PAID CALLS, separate from task count: with votes>1 they differ, and the number anyone asking 'what did this cost' wants is this one.
claims.why: The 'paid_calls' key (line 402) is set to counts['calls'], which increments per vote (line 338), not per task.

claims.text: a callback must not kill the queue
claims.why: The on_result callback is wrapped in try/except that catches all exceptions and passes (lines 381-383).

claims.text: the budget ledger prices reservations at a deliberate worst-case, so a ledger total is a ceiling and never an invoice.
claims.why: The comment refers to the budget ledger's pricing policy, which is implemented in another module (..budget). This chunk does not contain that logic.

observations.what: Guard error message includes guard_error but no traceback.
Callback exceptions are silently ignored with pass.
